title: Ding Dong Merrily on High
description: George Ratcliffe Woodward's carol of the Christmas bells, to the old French dance tune "Branle de l'Official", in Charles Wood's harmony from The Cambridge Carol Book (1924), for 2 to 4 singers: all three verses, each followed twice by the long rolling "Gloria, Hosanna in excelsis!". The alto sings mostly a sixth under the tune in the verses, and in the Gloria the lower parts hold one note a chord while the tune runs, each part breathing at its own place.

credits.words: George Ratcliffe Woodward (The Cambridge Carol Book, 1924)
credits.tune: "Branle de l'Official", from Thoinot Arbeau's Orchésographie (1589)
credits.arrangement: Charles Wood's harmony (The Cambridge Carol Book, 1924), adapted by Stackapella

licence.words: public domain: George Ratcliffe Woodward died 1934
licence.tune: public domain: the dance tune "Branle de l'Official" printed in Thoinot Arbeau's Orchésographie (Langres, 1589; Arbeau died 1595), as Charles Wood (died 1926) set it to Woodward's words
licence.arrangement: Charles Wood's four-part harmony, signed "(C.W.)" on the page (public domain: Wood died 1926), adapted. Kept: Wood's tune note for note, a tone lower; his bass in the verses; his chords on almost every beat, some in another position (the one changed chord is on "bells", below); his rests for the lower parts on the first beat of bars 9, 11 and 13 (their breaths in the Gloria); and his alto's quaver run, tenor and bass in bar 10. Changed for 2 to 4 beginners (pitches as written here, in A-flat): in the verses the alto sings mostly a sixth under the tune, C4, E-flat4, D-flat4, C4, B-flat3, A-flat3, G3 under "Ding dong! mer-ri-ly on high" where Wood's alto has E-flat4, E-flat4, F4, F4, D-flat4, D-flat4, B-flat3 (a bare fourth under the tune on "Ding" and on the held "high"), A-flat3, D-flat4, D-flat4, C4, B-flat3 under "in heav'n the bells are" (his E-flat4, E-flat4, D-flat4, B-flat3, E-flat4) and C4 under each line's last two notes (his E-flat4); the tenor exchanges, E-flat3 for his C4 and A-flat3 on "Ding dong!", D-flat3 for his B-flat3 and A-flat3 under "ly on", E-flat3 for his G3 and A-flat3 under "high" and "in", and A-flat3 for his C4 at each line's end; so Wood's suspended chord on "bells" becomes A-flat over E-flat (alto C4, tenor A-flat3) before the same E-flat chord. In the Gloria the lower parts sing one held note a chord where Wood writes quavers (bars 9 and 11 to 14): the bass G2, A-flat2, C3, his G3, A-flat3, C3 an octave down (bar 9), A-flat2 held for his F3 (bar 11), B-flat2 held where he returns to G2 (bar 12, so the leading tone is not doubled), and E-flat3, C3, E-flat3, C3 under "Glo- ri- a, Ho-" where he climbs E-flat3, F3, G3, A-flat3 (bar 14); the alto E-flat4 held through bar 9 (over his A-flat4 on its last beat), E-flat4, F4, E-flat4 (bar 11, from his E-flat4, D-flat4 quavers, C4, F4: the F4 gives three singers the F minor chord's root), D-flat4, C4, D-flat4, B-flat3 (bar 12), C4, A-flat3, D-flat4 (bar 13, his own notes, held into bar 14), then C4, G3, A-flat3 for "ri- a, Ho-"; the tenor B-flat3, A-flat3 (bar 9), G3, then F3 held, then E-flat3 (bars 11 and 12), E-flat3, F3, A-flat3 (bar 13) and B-flat3, A-flat3, E-flat3, E-flat3 (bar 14); so no two voices move in octaves or fifths and the duet keeps a third or sixth on most strong beats. Bars 15 and 16, which Wood sets as bars 3 and 4, are sung with the verse's changes. Breaths written in for beginners: each verse line's and each Gloria's last note gives up a beat and a quarter, and in the Gloria the tune breathes after the first half beat of the dotted notes in bars 12 and 14 ("(o)-" and "ri-" start its new lines) while the lower parts sing on, and the lower parts breathe in Wood's rests while the tune sings on. Accepted exceptions: the lower parts hold "Glo-" ("(o)-" after their breaths) through the Gloria on one note a chord, a melisma, as every voice on Wood's page sings the word; the duet bare on a few weak beats (a fourth on "dong!", fifths on "in", "the" and the Gloria's "Ho-", and an octave E-flat under the tune on the second and fourth beats of bar 9, Wood's own on the second); the chord on "high" without its fifth in four parts (tenor and bass both on E-flat3, so the alto can take the third for the duet); the duet's quaver fourths in Wood's bar 10 run, its octave D-flat on bar 10's fourth beat and octave B-flat on bar 12's, its fifths on "na" and on bar 13's fourth beat, and its tritones G4 over D-flat4 on bar 12's third beat and bar 14's first (the second the alto's held D-flat4); the alto and tenor in unison on B-flat3 for "are"
licence.source: Charles Wood and George Ratcliffe Woodward, eds., The Cambridge Carol Book, being Fifty-two Songs for Christmas, Easter, and Other Seasons (London: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge; New York and Toronto: The Macmillan Co., 1924), No. VIII, "Ding dong! merrily on high". The music, "Tune, Branle de l'Official from Thoinot Arbeau's Orchésographie, 1588 (C.W.)", words signed "G. R. Woodward", in four parts on two staves in B-flat, 4/4, verse 1 under the treble staff and verses 2 and 3 under the bass, the Gloria in repeat marks, written here a tone lower in A-flat, read from an undated S.P.C.K. page of the same setting, scanned at IMSLP (imslp.org/wiki/Ding_Dong_Merrily_on_High_(Wood,_Charles), file IMSLP263626, catalogued there "S.P.C.K., n.d. [1910]"; the page carries no date or number); the words as printed in the book's 1924 words edition ("3d. net", its verso "Music Edition. 68 pp. ... Printed in Great Britain 1924", the Bodleian Library copy stamped 6 February 1925), No. VIII, p. 10, read from the scan at commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_Cambridge_Carol_Book.djvu (page 13): all three verses, "priests" and "song" as that edition prints them (the music page has "priest" and "Song"), the Gloria after each verse, twice, as the music's repeat marks show. Arbeau's own printing was seen, not compared note by note: Orchésographie (Langres, 1589), archive.org/details/danceman219, leaf n197 (the heading "B. de l'Official" and the dance) and n198 ("Continuation de l'air"; the page with the air's opening is not in this scan). Wood died 1926, Woodward 1934, Arbeau 1595
